nflrest

Compute team rest disparities, travel metrics, and date-aware body-clock shifts for NFL games, then combine them into a composite schedule-advantage score. Data come from nflverse / nflreadr.

Status: core analysis implemented and tested. The vignette and written deliverables are still in progress.

Intended audience

nflrest is for analysts, students, and sports researchers who want reproducible rest and travel metrics without building their own data pipeline.

Installation

Not yet on CRAN. Install from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jbaker12/MSDS457_Final_Project")

The repository is named MSDS457_Final_Project; the package it contains is nflrest.

Usage 

library(nflrest)

# Rest disparity, short weeks, and byes
rest <- calculate_rest_disparity(nfl_schedules_sample)

# One row per team-game with travel miles. The default itinerary model
# chains consecutive road games; use trip_model = "round_trip" for the
# older out-and-back version.
travel <- calculate_travel_miles(nfl_schedules_sample)

# Team-season travel totals
summarize_travel_miles(travel)

# Signed clock shifts and east/west body-clock penalties
shifts <- flag_time_zone_shifts(nfl_schedules_sample)

# Composite score; positive values favor the home team
advantage <- calculate_schedule_advantage(nfl_schedules_sample)

# Season totals and ranks
season <- calc_schedule_disparity(nfl_schedules_sample)

# Compare outcomes for disadvantaged teams; min_edge drops tiny edges
eval_rest_impact(nfl_schedules_sample, advantage = advantage, min_edge = 0.5)

# Team-by-venue travel heatmap
plot_travel_matrix(travel)

nfl_schedules_sample contains the 2024 and 2025 schedules with kickoff times, final scores, closing spreads, rest, and venue columns, so these examples run without a network connection.

The functions accept any data frame with the required columns, not only the bundled sample. calculate_rest_disparity() needs game_id, gameday, home_team, and away_team; calculate_travel_miles() needs game_id, home_team, and away_team, and uses stadium_id, location, week, and gameday when present. flag_time_zone_shifts() uses gametime when present and assumes 1:00 p.m. Eastern otherwise. A schedule from nflreadr::load_schedules() with those columns can be passed directly.

Live ingestion is available through the optional nflreadr dependency:

schedule <- load_nfl_schedule(2024:2025)
clear_nflrest_cache()

The first call needs network access; later calls reuse an in-memory cache. Install nflreadr separately because it is a suggested dependency.

Composite score

calculate_schedule_advantage() converts each component to points and sums them:

  • rest: 0.25 points per day of rest disparity
  • travel: 0.5 points per 1,000 miles of extra travel
  • time zone: 0.35 points per hour of body-clock penalty

Travel disparity is the away team’s miles minus the home team’s; time-zone disparity is the away team’s penalty minus the home team’s. All weights are arguments, and the raw parts are returned with the score. The defaults are a starting point, not fitted values; eval_rest_impact() is the check against outcomes. A missing part, such as rest in a season opener, counts as zero and shows up in components_missing.

Assumptions

  • Rest is calendar days between a team’s games within a season. Season openers are NA because the package does not invent a prior game; nflverse reports 7 days for openers.
  • Home games are zero travel miles. Neutral-site games charge both teams a trip.
  • Travel is great-circle distance from the team’s home airport to the venue, not actual flight routing. The default itinerary model chains road games in adjacent weeks and resets on a bye; the "round_trip" model treats every road game as an independent out-and-back trip and overstates multi-game road stretches.
  • Time-zone shifts use the scheduled kickoff instant and IANA time zones, so daylight-saving changes are handled. Eastward shifts receive a larger default body-clock penalty than westward shifts.
  • Injury evaluation depends on an injury report supplied by the user; no injury data are bundled.
  • Historical team abbreviations (for example OAK, SD, STL) are not yet mapped to airport rows.

Bundled data

Dataset Rows What it is
nfl_schedules_sample 570 2024-2025 schedule with kickoff, score, spread, rest, and venue columns
nfl_airports 32 Each team’s home airport, coordinates, and time zone
nfl_stadiums 37 NFL and neutral-site venues with coordinates and time zones
